neighbours.label: the word right before a perfect 'have' (may have, claims to have, seems to have)
fire: Investigators think the fire may have started in the kitchen.
The suspect claims to have been at home all evening.
Some of the files might have been lost during the move.
She seems to have forgotten our meeting entirely.
The bridge could have collapsed without the extra supports.
He pretends to have read every book on the shelf.
The letter must have arrived while we were away.
The company appears to have overstated its profits.
quiet: Investigators think the fire started in the kitchen.
The suspect says he was at home all evening.
Some of the files were lost during the move.
The bridge stayed up thanks to the extra supports.
He says he reads every book on the shelf.
The letter arrived while we were away.
The company overstated its profits last year.

notes: Card flags broad (2.0%). Top examples are mixed (plenty more, Arabic التي); probing showed 'claims to have' strongest.
